Welcome to Sacred Heart Catholic Primary School
Welcome
On behalf of the children, staff and governors, I would like to offer you a warm welcome to Sacred Heart Catholic Primary School. I hope that you will find our website clear and informative and that it gives you an insight into the vibrant life at our school.
Sacred Heart is a friendly and happy school where every child is valued and encouraged to develop to their full potential. It is a place where staff, children, parents, governors and parish work together to provide a safe and caring environment. As a Christian community in the Catholic tradition, the Gospel values of love, friendship, inclusivity, respect and forgiveness are key to the nurture that each child receives. Our school motto, ‘Excellence through Faith and Learning’, reflects this and the children are encouraged to develop in their faith whilst engaging in a rich and varied curriculum focused on offering all children the skills, enthusiasm and resilience that they will need in order to embrace future opportunities and the experiences of later life.
Visitors to our school are always welcome. If you require any further information or you would like your child to join our school, please make an appointment to come and see the school in action. I look forward to meeting you

Admissions & Appeals Arrangements
Parish Boundaries Map
How parents can apply for a school place:
Apply online at: https://www.eastsussex.gov.uk/education-learning/schools/apply-for-a-school-place
(Admissions and Transport team on 0300 330 9472 for a paper application)
Complete and return a completed 'Supplementary Information Form' (SIF) to the School Office (not the Local Authority) with all the relevant documentation eg. Certificate of baptism. SIF forms can be found below.
Further Information
The Governing Board of Sacred Heart Catholic Primary School is responsible for determining the admission arrangements of the school, including the priority of admissions to the school when the school is oversubscribed (when we receive more applications than spaces available).
Our criteria can be found on our Admissions Policy.
Please note: All year groups have a PAN number of 30.
Admission Arrangements 2025 - 2026 - IN YEAR ADMISSIONS ONLY
The Governing Body will consider whether classes have any vacancies and if so, whether they are able to offer a place.
Once confirmed, the school will inform East Sussex County Council (ESCC) and the school will contact you to let you know the outcome of your application.

Appeals
If the School has more applications than places, parents whose child has not been allocated a place may appeal. Appeals will be considered by an Independent Appeal Panel set up in accordance with the Department for Education Appeals code.
The deadline for receipt of an in year appeal: You should submit your appeal within 25 school days of the date of a letter confirming the decision to refuse your application.
Appeals will be heard within 30 school days of your letter being received. Parents will be given at least 10 school days written notice of the date of the appeal hearing.
Appeals should be submitted to:
The Chair of the Board of Governors,Sacred Heart Catholic Primary School,HastingsEast SussexTN35 5NA
Any additional information in support of an appeal should be submitted at least 7 working days before the date of the hearing. Additional submissions (additional evidence to support your appeal) received after this deadline will still be forwarded on, but it will be for the Independent Appeal Panel to decide whether to accept any submissions received after the deadline.
A decision letter will be sent from the school within 5 days of the hearing.
Further information can be found below:
ESCC Appeals Information

Waiting Lists
Where an applicant is offered a school place following an in-year application, and the offer is accepted, arrangements should be made for the child to start school as soon as possible, particularly where the child is out of school.
If your child is not offered a place, you can add their name to a waiting list. Waiting lists are ranked according to each school’s admission criteria. Please note that we cannot give any indication of timescales for the availability of places.

Educational Visits
During the academic year, class outings are arranged suited to the topics covered by their class curriculum.

Carroty Wood
In Year 5, the children participate in a residential trip to Carroty Wood, Tonbridge.
In early May, whilst their child is in Year 4, Parents/Carers are invited to attend an initial meeting/presentation and given the opportunity to ask questions. Once numbers of children wishing to attend are confirmed, we are able to set the cost of the trip and details are sent out to parents with information regarding the activities, accommodation and overall cost, including suggested payment plan.
Permission, Health, Medical and Pocket Money forms, together with a full Kit List are sent out a few months before the trip.
Final details regarding transport, departure and return journeys, emergency contact numbers are also sent out.

Prospective Parents' Information
Starting School Reception – September 2026
Reception Class Numbers
If your child was born between:
1st September 2021 and 31st August 2022 (September 2026 intake)
1st September 2022 and 31st August 2023 (September 2027 intake)
In-year Admissions
What are In Year Admissions?
You can make an in-year application if your child needs to join a school outside of the normal admissions round - for example, if you move house and your child can no longer attend their current school.
How parents can apply for a school place
If you want to apply for an In-Year admission to Sacred Heart Catholic Primary School you need to complete:
The East Sussex In Year Application Form
The online ESCC Application Form can be found here: eastsussex.gov.uk/admissions
[Note: If you are not able to apply online please contact the ESCC Admissions and Transport team on 0300 330 9472 for a paper application.]
The School’s Supplementary Information Form (SIF)
The SIF is available here.
Who processes your application?
The governing body is the admissions authority for Sacred Heart Catholic Primary School and has responsibility for admissions to the school, including setting the priority of admissions when the school is oversubscribed.
The governing body will consider whether it has any vacancies and if so, whether they are able to offer a place. The school will confirm to East Sussex County Council (ESCC) as soon as possible. The school will contact you to let you know the outcome of your application.
When will parents be notified of the outcome of their application?
Upon receipt of an In Year application, the school aim to notify parents of the outcome of the application in writing within 10 school days. However, it might take up to 15 school days. You must respond to any offer of a place within ten school days.
The right to appeal
If you are refused a place at any school you applied for, you have the right to make an appeal to an independent appeal panel. Where an application is refused, the school will set out the reason for refusal.
For applications for In Year Admissions, appeals must be heard within 30 school days of the appeal being lodged. If parents wish to appeal, they must set out the grounds for appeal in writing.
Accepting a place
Where an applicant is offered a school place following an in-year application, and the offer is accepter, arrangements should be made for the child to start school as soon as possible, particularly where the child is out of school.
Waiting List
If your child is not offered a place, you can add their name to a waiting list. Waiting lists are ranked according to each school’s admission criteria. Your child’s position on a waiting list may go down as well as up, for example, if other children with greater priority according to the school’s admission criteria are added to the list.
Note: A hard copy of this online page is available on request for parents who don’t have internet access
